title: Use security models to reason about allowed information flow: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: Which model objective explains the proposed information-flow rule?
focalInsight: A model is selected by confidentiality, integrity, conflict, or transaction objective and needs enforcement.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Security Model
nodes.definition: Formal policy model describing permitted access or information flow.
nodes.detail: Formal policy model describing permitted access or information flow.
nodes.decision: Choose a model by the property and rule the system must enforce.
nodes.failureExample: A diagram names a model but no label, transaction, or workflow enforces it.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: A model protects only when implementation enforces its rule.

nodes.label: Bell Lapadula
nodes.definition: Confidentiality model using labels, including no read up and no write down.
nodes.detail: Confidentiality model using labels, including no read up and no write down.
nodes.decision: Use when preventing disclosure across classification levels is the primary objective.
nodes.failureExample: A secret-cleared user writes a secret finding into an unclassified report.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: For confidentiality flow: no read up; no write down.

nodes.label: Biba
nodes.definition: Integrity model that resists contamination from lower-integrity sources.
nodes.detail: Integrity model that resists contamination from lower-integrity sources.
nodes.decision: Use when trusted data or decisions must not be corrupted by less-trusted input.
nodes.failureExample: A high-integrity ledger imports unreviewed web data directly.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: For integrity flow: no read down; no write up.

nodes.label: Clark Wilson
nodes.definition: Integrity model based on well-formed transactions and separation of duties.
nodes.detail: Integrity model based on well-formed transactions and separation of duties.
nodes.decision: Use for controlled business processes where only authorized transformations may change data.
nodes.failureExample: A clerk edits account balances directly outside an approved transaction.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Protect integrity through constrained transactions and role separation.

nodes.label: Brewer Nash
nodes.definition: Conflict-of-interest model that restricts access after a user sees competing clients’ data.
nodes.detail: Conflict-of-interest model that restricts access after a user sees competing clients’ data.
nodes.decision: Use when commercial conflict classes govern information access.
nodes.failureExample: A consultant reads one bidder’s plans, then requests a competitor’s plans.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Prior access can create the conflict that later access must respect.

nodes.label: Star Property
nodes.definition: A model-specific information-flow constraint often called a star rule.
nodes.detail: A model-specific information-flow constraint often called a star rule.
nodes.decision: Identify the model and protected property before applying the rule.
nodes.failureExample: A learner treats “star property” as a universal access-control rule.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: The star rule needs its model context; it is not a stand-alone answer.

nodes.label: Integrity
nodes.definition: Assurance that information and processing remain accurate, complete, and authorized.
nodes.detail: Assurance that information and processing remain accurate, complete, and authorized.
nodes.decision: Prioritize when corruption, unauthorized change, or contaminated input is the harm.
nodes.failureExample: An approved invoice value can be altered by an unrestricted service account.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Integrity asks whether the change is authorized and trustworthy.

nodes.label: Confidentiality
nodes.decision: Prioritize when labels, audiences, or disclosure consequences govern the decision.
nodes.failureExample: A lower-cleared recipient receives a higher-classification export.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Confidentiality asks who may learn the information.

nodes.label: Information Flow
nodes.definition: Movement of information between subjects, objects, labels, or trust levels.
nodes.detail: Movement of information between subjects, objects, labels, or trust levels.
nodes.decision: Trace read, write, transformation, replication, and export paths.
nodes.failureExample: A sanitized report inherits hidden high-side fields during export.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Assess the flow, not only the source object.
